requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The persistent pwquality policy sets minlen=12, PAM invokes pam_pwquality, and an 11-character password was rejected both before and after reboot while a compliant password passed.

requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to use at least three character classes.
requirements.summary: The persistent pwquality policy sets minclass=3, PAM invokes pam_pwquality, and a 16-character single-class password was rejected both before and after reboot while a four-class password passed.

overall_summary: Both password-complexity outcomes are satisfied, persist across reboot, and have coherent configuration and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide node-restart protocol was completed successfully and independently corroborated by lifecycle observations.
limitations: Behavioral testing used pwscore rather than an end-to-end password-change transaction. PAM integration was directly observed, so this is a minor evidence limitation rather than an unmet outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the pwquality drop-in was the required implementation; temporary output files used for bounded checks were removed; and the reboot-related transient unit was necessary for the mandatory restart protocol. Post-executor observations show no failed services, damaged package state, unexpected listeners, or abandoned test files. The restart protocol was strong: it captured a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID, recovered system state, persistent policy, and repeated functional checks. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the reboot.
